events.title: Bulgaria Adopts The Euro
events.summary: Bulgaria adopted the euro on January 1, 2026, becoming the 21st member of the euro area.
events.context: The change followed the Council of the European Union's 2025 approval of Bulgaria's accession to the euro area and fixed the conversion from the Bulgarian lev to the euro.
events.whyItMatters: The adoption expanded the eurozone and marked a major monetary integration step for Bulgaria and the European Union.

media.alt: Suggested image: euro banknotes or Bulgarian central bank/euro changeover imagery.
media.caption: Bulgaria entered the euro area at the start of 2026.

events.detailMarkdown:
On January 1, 2026, the euro entered circulation in Bulgaria. The European Central Bank described the change as bringing the number of euro-area member states to 21.

The event matters as a monetary and institutional milestone: Bulgaria's central bank joined the Eurosystem, and the country moved from the lev to the shared European currency.

sources.notes: Confirms the January 1, 2026 adoption and euro-area membership.

events.title: Cyprus Begins Presidency Of The Council Of The European Union
events.summary: Cyprus assumed the Presidency of the Council of the European Union for the first half of 2026.
events.context: The rotating presidency gives an EU member state a central role in chairing Council work and brokering legislative priorities.
events.whyItMatters: The presidency placed Cyprus in a visible coordinating role during debates over EU autonomy, enlargement, competitiveness, and the next long-term EU budget.

media.alt: Suggested image: Cyprus Presidency or Council of the European Union visual identity.
media.caption: Cyprus chaired Council work during the first half of 2026.

events.detailMarkdown:
Cyprus held the rotating Presidency of the Council of the European Union from January 1 to June 30, 2026.

The presidency programme framed the period around a more autonomous European Union, open to the world, and emphasized issues including competitiveness, rule of law, enlargement, and long-term budget negotiations.
